targetText: The more intense national labour, therefore, as compared with the less intense, produces in the same time more value, which expresses itself in more money.
summary: National differences in wages: how differences in labour intensity and productivity shape global wage rates.
explanation: Wage levels vary between countries due to historical standards of living, training costs, and national productivity. More productive and intensive national labour produces greater value per hour on the world market, which translates into higher nominal wages even while the rate of surplus-value extracted by capital may be equal or higher.
context: Part VI, Chapter 22: National Differences of Wages
